- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative, model fails to mean-revert; force a moderate downward correction in next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to align with actual momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently neutral or mixed, model tends to drift toward historical mean; apply mean-reversion bias toward 30-day average of prior 10–15 days.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model overestimates; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
